laws_and_bills.name: S6394B / A9086 New York State Sustainable Data Centers Act
laws_and_bills.what: Data centers of 20 MW+ must file energy, emissions, water, waste heat and jobs reports with the PSC 180 days before construction, plus public hearings and annual reports; fines up to $10,000/day; bars utility discounts tied to fossil fuel power deals; renewable targets for data center power (1/3 by 2030, 2/3 by 2035, all by 2040). Amended and recommitted to Senate Energy and Telecommunications Committee 2026-05-30.

laws_and_bills.name: ECL 19-0331 Moratorium on air permit issuance and renewal (proof-of-work crypto mining at fossil fuel plants)
laws_and_bills.what: For two years from its effective date, DEC may not issue new air permits, or renewals that increase power used for mining, for fossil-fuel power plants supplying behind-the-meter power to proof-of-work cryptocurrency mining. Passed as S6486D/A7389C in June 2022.

laws_and_bills.name: Executive Order 62 (Hochul): temporary statewide moratorium on data centers
laws_and_bills.what: This is 'New York's data center moratorium'. Signed 2026-07-14. DEC pauses discretionary permits for data centers of 50 MW+ whose applications were not complete by 2026-07-14, until the DPS-led GEIS is done (no later than 2027-07-14 per law firm summaries). Exempts local permits and data centers mainly for manufacturing, research, education or medical care. Also orders a DPS Data Center Interconnection Working Group, a possible Grid Acceleration Fund, and an ESD Community Investment Framework.

laws_and_bills.name: S10642 / A11560 Responsible Data Center Development Act
laws_and_bills.what: One-year DEC permit moratorium for data centers of 20 MW+, then hearings, environmental impact reports, separate PSC rate classes for 20 MW+, renewable targets, host community benefits and labor standards. Passed Senate 43-17 on 2026-06-04 (substituted for A11560). Governor acted by executive order instead; no signature found.

laws_and_bills.name: S9182-A / A10852-A ban on data center subsidies
laws_and_bills.what: Would bar all subsidies to data centers: state and local sales tax breaks, property tax abatements and NYPA low-cost power.

laws_and_bills.name: Governor's proposal to repeal data center sales tax exemptions and bar IDA breaks for hyperscale (50 MW+)
laws_and_bills.what: Part of the September 2026 Community Investment Framework; Hochul wants to end the sales tax exemption for large data centers and block IDAs from giving property, sales and mortgage tax breaks to 50 MW+ data centers, possibly in the next budget.

local_rules.what: Proposed Local Law P-2 of 2026: temporary moratorium on 'certain high energy use facilities' while the City reviews its zoning. Introduced by Mayor Hughes 2026-10-01; public hearing 2026-10-15. Whether it names data centers or crypto mining is in a linked PDF not read.
Three-year moratorium on new data centers (reported as those over 20 MW, to July 2029), passed unanimously after Treetop floated a 1 GW project.
One-year data center moratorium after a project was planned on former farmland.
Town board voted 3-2 on 2026-09-26 against a local data center moratorium (NCCS/NYDIG project).

dockets.what: Energize NY Development proceeding on large-load (data center) interconnection reforms and cost allocation, opened 2026-02-12 after the governor's State of the State. Under EO 62 the PSC issued a SEQRA positive declaration and a Draft Scope for a Generic Environmental Impact Statement on data centers and large loads on 2026-09-17; comments due 2026-10-20. NYISO queue had 48 large-load projects over 11 GW as of January 2026 (governor).

incentives.name: Sales tax exemption for internet data centers (2000 law) and local IDA tax breaks
incentives.law: N.Y. Tax Law 1115(a)(37) (internet data center exemption); NCSL's 2026 table also cites Tax Law 1115(y)
incentives.what: Tax Law 1115(a)(37) exempts from state and local sales tax tangible personal property sold to a person operating an internet data center in New York for use in that center (paragraph text read 2026-10-15). County and town IDAs also grant property, sales and mortgage tax breaks (e.g., Stream asked Genesee County IDA for $1.46B). Governor proposes repeal for large data centers.
